title: A Fokker-Planck approach to a stochastic multiplicative wealth model with taxation and redistribution
authors: Iago Nascimento Barros, Marcelo Lobato Martins, Celia Anteneodo
abstract: We develop a Fokker-Planck description of the dynamics of wealth distribution in a stochastic multiplicative economic growth model with taxation and redistribution, as introduced by P.M.C. de Oliveira. Extending the original formulation, our theoretical framework includes general redistribution protocols, encompassing a broad class of state-dependent transfer mechanisms. As a particular case, we investigate a two-state protocol designed to emulate conditional cash transfer programs. Analytical expressions for the stationary wealth distributions are derived, revealing how the interplay between multiplicative noise, taxation, and redistribution shapes the emergence of inequality. The theoretical results are corroborated by agent-based simulations. To quantify and compare the impact of the different protocols, we employ the Gini index as a measure of inequality. Our analysis highlights how specific nonuniform redistribution schemes can significantly mitigate wealth disparities.
summary: This paper applies statistical physics tools, specifically Fokker-Planck equations, to analyze how wealth inequality evolves in an economy subject to taxes and redistribution. By comparing uniform versus nonuniform transfer protocols, the authors demonstrate that targeted redistribution can effectively stabilize the system and reduce measured economic disparities like the Gini index.
main_problem: The study develops a Fokker-Planck description for wealth distribution dynamics under stochastic multiplicative growth, incorporating taxation and general redistribution protocols.
main_result: Nonuniform redistribution schemes can significantly mitigate wealth disparities by stabilizing the stationary state compared to simple uniform models. The analysis suggests statistical properties might exhibit universality despite specific policy details.
method: The authors use continuous-time limits derived from discrete stochastic processes, leading to Fokker-Planck Equations (FPEs) for the probability density function of rescaled wealth.
model_or_system: The model describes a population's wealth evolution ($W_{i,t}$) through multiplicative noise, taxation ($	au$), and state-dependent redistribution ($	ext{r}_{i,t}$). The analysis focuses on the rescaled wealth $y_t$ governed by an associated SDE/FPE.
key_observables: Gini index (measure of inequality), stationary wealth distribution $P_{y,st}(y)$, and moments $\langle y^n angle$.
important_parameters: Taxation rate ($	au$), noise strength ($s$), redistribution parameters ($ eta$, $y_c$), and the exponent $\alpha$ governing the tail behavior.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field closure for large populations ($N 	o \infty$) and assumes specific functional forms for redistribution kernels (e.g., uniform or CCT limit).
figures_summary: Figures compare simulated and theoretical stationary PDFs for uniform redistribution, showing agreement, and illustrate the relaxation of variance over time.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from deriving the general Fokker-Planck equation for wealth dynamics to analyzing specific cases (uniform vs. nonuniform redistribution). It derives analytical forms for the stationary PDF and calculates inequality metrics like the Gini index for comparison.
why_interesting: While purely economic, the mathematical framework—using FPEs, stochastic processes, and steady-state analysis to model non-equilibrium distributions—is highly analogous to modeling energy or particle density in complex many-body systems far from equilibrium.
